label: Trial 1 completion — source access retest; RSP, RAISE, EU AI Act, GPAI Code, Frontier AI EO, China AI Law

discovery.area: Anthropic (lab, B4) — policy text and compliance documents (retest)
discovery.summary: With access restored I read the RSP v3.4 policy PDF in full, the v3.0 PDF, the Frontier Compliance Framework v2 (Trust Center; needed a headless browser) and Anthropic's Dec 2025 SB 53 post. Every change found is an update to the existing rsp entry, so no new entry is proposed.
queries: anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy (re-fetched; lists v3.4 as current; no newer version as of 2026-10-10)
Anthropic "Frontier Compliance Framework" SB 53 RAISE (web search for leads)
trust.anthropic.com Frontier AI Compliance section (headless Chromium)
discovery.limits: Other labs were not searched; that is outside this trial. The Feb and Aug 2026 Risk Reports and system cards were not read, so implementation evidence and elicitation practice were not checked.

candidates.name: RSP v3 structure (thresholds table, ASLs only for current safeguards, competitor-dependent delay commitments)
candidates.reason: Replaces the ASL-ladder and unconditional-pause wording on rsp.

candidates.name: Halting commitments under RSP v3 (Appendix A)
candidates.reason: Delay commitments now depend on competitor scenarios.

candidates.name: Frontier Compliance Framework v2 (effective 24 Jul 2026)
candidates.result: update to existing entry (context) — not a separate entry for now
candidates.reason: Anthropic's compliance document for California TFAIA and the summary of its EU Code Safety & Security Framework. It is distinct from the RSP. It is noted in the rsp context (P-0010) and the RAISE connection (P-0009), not given its own entry. Whether compliance frameworks deserve entries is a question for the baseline audit, because OpenAI, Google DeepMind and others likely publish equivalents.

candidates.name: RSP Noncompliance Reporting and Anti-Retaliation Policy
candidates.result: screened out — minor; note for baseline
candidates.reason: Unchanged from trial 1: an internal compliance policy. The v3.4 governance section (S-0006 §4) already commits to noncompliance reporting and anti-retaliation.

discovery.area: New York (B2 represented state) — RAISE Act as amended
discovery.summary: Read the enacted RAISE Act (Chapter 699 of 2025) and the chapter amendment (S8828, Chapter 96 of 2026) on nyassembly.gov. nysenate.gov, the map's current link, serves a Cloudflare bot challenge to automated clients; that is the website's block, not the environment's. The existing ny-raise description checks out.
queries: RAISE Act chapter amendment 2026 bill number (web search for leads)
discovery.limits: Only the transparency, incident-reporting, penalty and effective-date provisions were read. DFS office regulations and the reported Sep 2026 developer registration (a search lead) were not checked.

candidates.name: RAISE Act chapter amendment (Ch. 96 of 2026)
candidates.result: update to existing entry — none needed
candidates.reason: Already reflected in ny-raise (Mar 27, 2026 amendment; effective Jan 1, 2027).

candidates.name: DFS office registration of large frontier developers (reported Sep 2026)
candidates.reason: Seen only in search results. If confirmed, it is implementation of ny-raise, not a new mechanism. Check in the baseline audit.

discovery.area: EU (jurisdiction, B1) — retest of trial-1 leads with official sources
discovery.summary: All trial-1 EU leads were checked against official sources: the Official Journal, EUR-Lex and Commission pages, read by a research subagent and re-checked by Claude. The Digital Omnibus is confirmed. The Article 50 transparency code is adopted and is a candidate new entry, raised to the maintainer but not drafted.
queries: digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu: AI Act page, enforcement framework page, GPAI Code page (signatories), AI Office page
Commission pages on the code of practice on transparency of AI-generated content (policy page, 10 Jun 2026 news, 9 Jul 2026 adequacy opinion, 31 Jul 2026 signatories news)
GPAI Code Safety and Security chapter PDF
discovery.limits: EUR-Lex served empty HTTP 202 responses after the first retrievals (a website-side throttle, not the environment). The consolidated AI Act text was not retrieved. Items listed on the Commission AI Act page but not opened: the EU Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI (7 Jul 2026), the AI Office frontier expert findings (15 Jul 2026) and the Scientific Panel special meeting (5 Oct 2026).

candidates.name: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 27 Jul 2026)
candidates.reason: Moves high-risk application dates. Also adds AI Office powers, which are relevant to eu-aio in the baseline audit.

candidates.name: AI Office GPAI enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; GPAI fine cap €15M/3%
candidates.reason: The map overstated the cap and used the future tense.

candidates.name: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content (Art 50; final 10 Jun 2026; Commission adequacy 8 Jul 2026; AI Board 9 Jul 2026)
candidates.result: proposed coverage addition — not drafted; maintainer decision needed
candidates.reason: Meets RUBRIC §1: an identifiable text, material to GPAI and generative AI providers, attributable to the Commission and AI Office. It would sit in Layer 5 (voluntary code), like gpai-cop. Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI are reported Section 1 signatories (Commission news, 31 Jul 2026, read by the subagent only). Not drafted because a new entry needs layer, pow, coverage notes and connections decided together.

candidates.name: Commission guidelines on Article 50 (Jul 2026)
candidates.result: lead — context for the code above
candidates.reason: Interpretive guidance, not a separate mechanism.

candidates.name: AI Office GPAI Code 'Signatory Taskforce'
candidates.result: screened out as a separate entry
candidates.reason: Implementation forum of gpai-cop (unchanged from trial 1).

discovery.area: US federal (B1) — Frontier AI EO and CAISI (retest)
discovery.summary: Read EO 14409 in the Federal Register (govinfo PDF and FR API). The map's description of it as a CAISI-administered national-security review is wrong; corrected in P-0014 and P-0015. Found in passing: NIST has renamed CAISI to CAISSI.
queries: whitehouse.gov EO 14409 page and fact sheet (subagent)
Federal Register search for later EOs amending 14409 (subagent)
discovery.limits: federalregister.gov HTML pages and commerce.gov serve website bot challenges. The reported White House instruction for CAISI to halt public reports has no executive-branch source; a congressional letter only relays press reports. Implementation of the EO (benchmark, framework, clearinghouse) was not found.

candidates.name: EO 14409 (2 Jun 2026)
candidates.reason: Official text differs materially from the map.

candidates.name: CAISI renamed CAISSI (Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence), page modified 30 Sep 2026
candidates.result: lead — update to existing entry (caisi); outside this trial
candidates.reason: Follows EO 14434 (29 Sep 2026) on 'Super Intelligence' terminology, per the subagent. Queue for the baseline audit.

candidates.name: EO 14434 'Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence' (29 Sep 2026)
candidates.result: lead — screen in the baseline audit
candidates.reason: Read by the subagent only. A terminology order; whether it is material under RUBRIC §1 is undecided.

candidates.name: Reported halt of CAISI public model reports
candidates.reason: NIST published CAISI assessments in Jul and Sep 2026, so a blanket halt is not supported.
